svg.title: AMRScan
svg.desc: Four scenes. 1: a scan line passes along the chromosome of an E. coli cell; blaCTX-M-15, gyrA S83L and tet(A) light up and are added to a report as resistant calls for ceftriaxone, nalidixic acid and tetracycline, with the tool, database and input hashes recorded. 2: a random split draws test isolates from every population, a holdout keeps a whole lineage, country, project or period out; for most of the 24 drugs a random split overstated AUROC only slightly. 3: k-mers sampled at 1 in 200 cover gyrA S83L in 0 of 2,298 calls, and 2,295 of 2,298 at 1 in 50. 4: adding known mutations raises nalidixic acid holdout AUROC by 0.155 to 0.232.

g.text: Resistance calls you can trace back to the run,
tested on populations the model has not seen.

svg.text: Nextflow · NCBI AMRFinderPlus · 10,521 E. coli genomes · 26 countries

g.text: Every call recorded with how it was made
Test on genomes unlike the training data
Random split: test isolates from every population
Holdout: a whole lineage, country, project or period
For most of the 24 drugs a random split overstated AUROC
only slightly (median gap 0.005 to 0.025); a few drugs lost more.
Sampled k-mers can miss a point mutation
S83L calls covered by a sampled k-mer
covered at four times the density
Nalidixic acid AUROC under each holdout
